title: Acknowledgements
text: Acknowledgements In preparing this book I have been helped enormously by colleagues throughout the world who have shared their specialist knowledge with me, read and improved sections of the text, translated, and contributed new information. They include especially the following. Australia Peter Barrett, Anne and Les Dollin, Dr Josephine Flood, Trevor Weatherhead Belgium Professor Octaaf van Laere Brazil Professor Warwick Kerr, Professor Paulo Nogueira-Neto Bulgaria Professor Todor Simidchiev Canada John Corner, Alan King and historians whose help he enlisted, Robert W. Libraries – especially the Eva Crane Library of IBRA in Cardiff, the Moir Library in Edinburgh, and Buckinghamshire County Library: Chalfont St Peter Branch and the Reference Section at High Wycombe USA Elizabeth Buxton, Professor Harry Laidlaw, Wyatt Mangum, William Petch, Professor Nevin Weaver, Ralph Wilcoxen Vietnam Vincent Mulder, Nguyen Thu Hang Zimbabwe Peter Genge I am grateful to photographers and artists named in Figure captions for permission to reproduce their illustrations, and I hope that the few who could not be traced will not object to the use of their material. I owe a great deal to my colleague Penelope Walker who worked with me in compiling and organizing the book, improving its structure and clarity, and providing support in many other ways. And I much appreciate Sandra Braithwaite’s orderly work in processing the many drafts of text and tables. I valued the friendly co-operation of Colin Haycraft of Duckworth until his untimely death in 1994, and since then of Deborah Blake and Ray Davies. During my travels in different countries I received much hospitality and help in other ways from many people, including specialists in different subjects and translators – particularly for Asian and African languages. The visits were often arranged in conjunction with professional assignments to lecture or to advise on beekeeping, bee research or honey. The work on which much of the book is based could not have been done without the support and generosity of spirit of my husband James Crane, who died in 1978.
